claim: The binary arm of NullPropagatedOperands recurses into every SqlBinaryExpression with no operator filter, so AndAlso/OrElse operands are treated as null-propagating even though SQL NULL does not propagate through them (NULL OR TRUE = TRUE, NULL AND FALSE = FALSE); the optimization therefore drops a load-bearing IS NOT NULL guard and the CASE returns TRUE/FALSE where it must return NULL, producing silently wrong query results (including in WHERE, reaching ExecuteDelete/ExecuteUpdate). Reproduced by execution against SQLite plus a control run; the same exception is already guarded in ProcessNullNotNull at line 2314.
raw: #1 🔴 Critical: `NullPropagatedOperands` treats `AndAlso`/`OrElse` as null-propagating, producing silently wrong query results

claim: All five new theories build their WHEN results only from ~ (unary Not) and + (add/concat) — operators that genuinely propagate NULL — so the one operator family the optimization gets wrong (&&/||) is left untested, which is why the Critical defect ships green. The func.InstancePropagatesNullability arm (line 633) and SqlFunctionExpression argument propagation are likewise uncovered by any new test.
raw: #2 🟡 Medium: The unsound recursion arms have zero test coverage

claim: NullPropagatedOperands encodes an unstated soundness invariant ("E IS NULL implies expression IS NULL under SQL three-valued logic") with no summary comment, no reference to 3VL, no explanation of why the unary arm admits exactly Not/Negate/Convert, and no signal that adding an operator to SqlBinaryExpression.IsValidOperator obliges revisiting this function; VisitCase is protected virtual provider-extensibility surface so a provider can invalidate the assumption from outside the assembly.
raw: #3 🟡 Medium: `NullPropagatedOperands` encodes an unstated soundness invariant with no comment

claim: DropNotNullChecks returns SqlExpression? where null means "the remaining test is the constant TRUE", carried only by a trailing // true comment, while thirty lines earlier in the same method null carries the opposite meaning (a null elseResult means possibly NULL). A maintainer extending it to handle OrElse tests will reach for null as the "nothing left" value and silently invert the predicate, since under OR the identity element is FALSE.
raw: #4 🟢 Low: `null` return of `DropNotNullChecks` overloads "absent" with "vacuously TRUE"

claim: SqlConstantExpression violates the Equals/GetHashCode contract: GetHashCode uses HashCode.Combine(base.GetHashCode(), Value) (default hashing) while Equals does element-wise comparison for IList values, so two constants that compare equal can hash differently. Pre-existing, but the change gives it a live consumer via the new HashSet<SqlExpression> at SqlNullabilityProcessor.cs:580; impact is a missed optimization, never a wrong result.

The // issue #16050 marker, which flags asserted SQL as known-suboptimal, was left on Null_propagation_optimization5, _optimization6, and Select_null_propagation_optimization7 whose baselines this change rewrote to optimal form (also in TPCGearsOfWarQuerySqlServerTest.cs and TPTGearsOfWarQuerySqlServerTest.cs), so one marker now carries two meanings.

claim: No AssertSql override exists for any of the five new theories (0 occurrences of Is_not_null_optimizes), so on SQLite the feature has no SQL-shape regression coverage — the base theories only call AssertQuery, which cannot detect the optimization silently ceasing to fire.

claim: Claimed that ExpressionType.Coalesce is reachable as a SqlBinaryExpression from ?? and would likewise drop the guard; probed and refuted — ?? becomes a COALESCE SqlFunctionExpression with argumentsPropagateNullability [false,false] and the guard is preserved. Folded into finding #1's fix as a fail-closed recommendation rather than reported.

IsNull(elseResult) is false for an absent ELSE, so the optimization silently does not fire for ELSE-less CASEs even though CASE WHEN t THEN r END is semantically equivalent to ... ELSE NULL END. A missed optimization, not a soundness defect.

claim: NullPropagatedOperands eagerly builds a HashSet of every sub-expression of the result before checking whether the test contains any droppable IS NOT NULL, and SqlExpression.GetHashCode is recursive and uncached — O(m·depth) compile-time cost per single-WHEN CASE; a cheap early-out would remove it.
Unbounded recursion in both new local functions; judged pre-existing since every visitor in this 2000-line file recurses the same way and no new risk is introduced.
